author: fable-cursor
criterion: Crown edges are broken and leafy against the sky; no ball-shaped canopies.
note: Against the sky at B the mid-ground crowns are ball-shaped: each is one smooth rounded lobe of a single green tone stuck on a bare trunk, with a serrated but flat outline and no internal leaf structure. A patch of actual blue sky shows through at the top left. The house moss cap on the right is the one part of the frame where leaf clusters and broken edges do read, and it is a roof, not a crown. The reference's crowns at the same height are dense masses of small overlapping clusters whose edges break against the bright haze. Auto gates are met (leafGeometry laminae, leafCount 288607), so the laminae exist but the mid-distance crown LOD is not using them.
